flagged.evidence: The displayed right inequality is asserted for every integer n>=1 and at n=1 contains integral_0^1 dt/t. The cited integral theorem requires integrable real functions on a closed interval, while def-natural-logarithm says log has domain exactly (0,infinity); 1/t is not a real-valued integrable function on [0,1]. Thus this half of 1.1 is undefined. It is also the inequality called on in 2.1 to obtain E_N>=0, although that conclusion instead follows from the left inequality.

Step 1.1 says that repeatedly applying prop-odd-two-square-representations-correspond-under-doubling transports representations of 1 to those of every 2^a. That dependency begins, “Let m be a positive odd integer,” and only supplies a bijection from representations of such an m to those of 2m. After the first application the input is m=2, which is not odd, so it does not license the asserted repetition.

Step 2.1 attributes its full piecewise formula, including r_2(N)/4=0 when some q≡3 (mod 4) has odd exponent, to “Hackman Chapter K.III.1.” The cited K.III.1 theorem says only, “Assume that prime numbers q ≡ 3 (mod 4) only enter the factorization of N with even multiplicity,” and then gives the 4 product(e_j+1) count. It does not state or establish the odd-exponent zero case; that requires the earlier representation criterion.

Step 2.1 cites [[thm-product-rule]] to differentiate G(t)=t log t-t. The opened dependency is titled “The product rule: |A × B| = |A| |B|” and its Statement concerns cardinalities of finite Cartesian products, not the differential product rule. It cannot license G'(t)=log t.

Step 3.1 claims sum_{m>Y}1/m^2 <= sum_{m>Y}(1/(m-1)-1/m) <= 1/Y. For Y=1.99 (an allowed real value, e.g. x=1.99 and d=1), the left sum is sum_{m=2}^infty 1/m^2=pi^2/6-1≈0.644934, whereas 1/Y≈0.502513. Hence the displayed bound is false, even though a corrected constant-factor tail bound would suffice for the later O(1/Y) estimate.
